searchText: I believe <@!329594653097721856> is arguing that it should become an invalid opcode and revert/assert essentially. My counter to that is that `SENDALLETH` does a subset of what `SELFDESTRUCT` does, and there is value in adding a `SENDALLETH` opcode, so it is strictly better (IMO) to have `SELFDESTRUCT` become `SEND_ALLETH` than to make `SELFDESTRUCT` assert and then add a new opcode for `SENDALLETH`. It will make it so people who are using `SELFDESTRUCT` today to sweep an account will still be able to do so (at higher gas cost), so we will break fewer people. I would support a layered approach. For one fork or so both SELFDESTRUCT and SENDALLETH work, and solidity exposes their sendalleth mapping and marks selfdestruct as a lint error. After a transition period either selfdestruct becomes an invalid call, a no-op, or a SENDALLETH. For the last option we would want to add contract scanning code that would make _new_ deployments with SELFDESTRUCT fail. But what's tricky is that eth has never removed an opcode or precompiled contract, so it's unexplored territory. Maybe the cost of a SELFDESTRUCT could be increased to a higher cost. Combine this with the option of SENDALLETH, eliminating refunds, and Solidity lint errors we will get _mostly_ there. But the state delete still poses a verkle trie risk. Sharing for visibility: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-3300-phase-out-refunds/5434 Alternative to straight up removing refunds, which reduces their amount over ~1 year Basically GasToken holders upset that they won't abuse the network anymore Boo hoo I think a gradual incentive to clear out the inventory is better than a deadline and the preceding fire sale. I expect we would see more state cleanup in the gradual scenario. I do think we should get it, and then reGenesis done as soon as possible why do you think so? my intuition is we get more cleanup if it's not phased out State size is a red herring here anyway. We should optimize it through other means anyway, for which selfdestruct phase out may be a prerequisite So the sooner certain EVM vestiges are gone, the sooner we can do reGenesis and cut a lot of complexity from the clients Generally agree, although 1m blocks (~1y) seems _very_ long, especially given the "advance warning" w.r.t. this actually hitting mainnet. IMO if we're planning to, say, have another upgrade around Q4/Q1, we should aim to have the refund at 0 by then, and then we can maybe simplify a lot of code on the next fork. So, in other words, ~1 year from today seems fine, but not ~1 year from London hitting mainnet 😅 Need reGenesis to simplify, mind you We have block history to execute I feel like "regenesis" is combining together multiple concepts that are best separated... If we just want clients to be able to sync from block 11m and forget about history, that's one thing Zeroing out the state is another thing Strictly speaking we need the first, not the second (though I see value in both eventually) You mean shadowing and reconstructing from witnesses? yeah Yes, this thought occurred to me too Actually, the merge is already a natural regenesis in the first sense of the word (forgetting all previous history, at least on the eth1 side) Technically, first may be very quick to implement, just need to have standardized snapshot format right, just need to put the state on bittorrent in some standard format (I suspect it may be that turbogeth will propose one as pioneer, who knows) We have it on bittorrent already, but it's just libmdbx database, so cannot be deterministically reconstructed used in our bittorrent sync We do have a prototype of rlp+raw deterministic format which is geared towards batch packing and quick random access
